questions.q: What is the most important clue in Meridian Retail's six-month Instance Health trend, according to this lesson?
options: Average load time climbs gradually and accelerates as store count grows, with no single deployment lining up with the steepest jump
A single deployment caused an overnight cliff-edge regression in response time
Instance Health shows no change at all over the six months
The transaction volume actually fell as more stores went live
questions.explain: A gradual, accelerating climb with no matching deployment spike points toward a design that scales badly with volume, not one bad release.

questions.q: Why does the lesson build a named hypothesis list instead of jumping straight to a fix?
options: Applying a fix on a guess risks making things worse or hiding the real cause, so each candidate should be confirmed with real evidence first
A hypothesis list is only useful for live incidents, not performance investigations
There is never more than one real cause behind a slow instance
Fixes should always be applied before any diagnosis to save time
questions.explain: This mirrors Chapter 6's incident-response discipline: gather evidence and confirm hypotheses before changing production.

questions.q: Which chapter's diagnostic skill is the right first tool for the platform-wide, exactly-7 AM slowdown symptom?
options: Chapter 4 — instance health, semaphores, and scheduled job contention
Chapter 1 — slow forms and list views
Chapter 5 — integration and Flow troubleshooting
Chapter 2 — script performance patterns
questions.explain: An instance-wide slowdown tied to a sharp usage spike is exactly the semaphore-contention pattern Chapter 4 covers.

questions.q: Why might a single root cause, such as a missing index, explain more than one of Meridian Retail's reported symptoms?
options: The same slow query a list view relies on could also be the query a Script Include re-runs inside a loop for approvals
List views and Script Includes never share the same underlying queries
Missing indexes only ever affect list views, never scripts
Each symptom in this scenario must have its own completely unrelated cause
questions.explain: The lesson calls this overlap out explicitly as the reason not to stop investigating after confirming just the first hypothesis.

questions.q: What does Instance Health answer that a single slow-transaction log entry cannot, per Chapter 4's distinction referenced here?
options: Whether the instance as a whole is trending slower over time, not just whether one specific request was slow
The exact line of script code causing a delay
Whether a specific user's browser cache is out of date
The storage size of a specific table
questions.explain: Instance Health aggregates metrics across the whole instance over time, answering a trend question a single transaction record can't.
